articles.title: Manhoos' Taunts, Dowry Harassment Alleged: Uttarakhand Secretariat Official, Family Booked
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A case has been registered against a personal secretary at the Uttarakhand Secretariat and his family members over the alleged dowry death of his 27-year-old wife, Shristi Bhandari, a government school teacher, in Dehradun's Doiwala area.

body.html:
A case has been registered against a personal secretary at the Uttarakhand Secretariat and his family members over the alleged dowry death of his 27-year-old wife, Shristi Bhandari, a government school teacher, in Dehradun's Doiwala area.

Acting on a complaint filed by the victim's mother, Seema Bhandari, police on Thursday registered an FIR under Section 80(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which deals with dowry death, against Shristi's husband, Saurabh Khatri, his mother Parvina Devi, sister Charu Khatri and other unidentified family members.

According to the complaint, Shristi married Khatri in November last year and moved into her matrimonial home in Doiwala, around 20 km from Dehradun. Soon after the marriage, her husband and in-laws allegedly subjected her to physical and mental cruelty while demanding dowry.

In a 90-second video recorded before she took the drastic step, Shristi is seen crying and apologising to her mother. She says she had been suffering for the past six months and could no longer endure the situation. She also alleges that her in-laws repeatedly blamed her for incidents that occurred after her marriage and constantly called her "manhoos" (inauspicious).

Circle Officer (Doiwala) Vandana Verma said the victim was allegedly humiliated regularly by her husband's family. According to the officer, they referred to Shristi as "inauspicious" and "unlucky", claiming misfortunes began after her arrival. The family also allegedly blamed her for the death of her father-in-law, who had passed away after a prolonged illness.

The incident came to light after Seema Bhandari was unable to contact her daughter on July 28 and 29 and asked relatives living nearby to check on her. They found Shristi in a critical condition at a local hospital. By the time her mother reached Dehradun from Srinagar in Garhwal, Shristi had died while undergoing treatment.

#Uttarakhand #Dehradun #DowryDeath #CrimeNews #JusticeForShristi

articles.title: You Destroyed 12 Years of My Life': Husband Confronts Wife and Her Alleged Lover on Indore Street
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A dramatic confrontation between a husband, his wife and her alleged lover on a street in Indore has gone viral on social media, prompting a police inquiry into the incident.

body.html:
A dramatic confrontation between a husband, his wife and her alleged lover on a street in Indore has gone viral on social media, prompting a police inquiry into the incident.

According to reports, the husband allegedly caught his wife with another man after suspecting her movements for some time. A heated argument followed, during which the husband allegedly beat his wife with a belt.

The viral video shows the husband, dressed in a blue shirt, repeatedly hitting the woman with a belt, while the alleged lover, wearing a yellow T-shirt, is seen recording the incident on his mobile phone. The woman is also seen grabbing her husband's collar as bystanders intervene to calm the situation.

In the video, the visibly emotional husband can be heard accusing his wife of betraying their 12-year marriage. He alleges that he had been monitoring her activities and eventually caught her with the other man.

Police said they have taken cognisance of the viral video and launched an inquiry. Senior officials from Vijay Nagar police station are verifying the location of the incident and the identities of those involved.

Further action will be taken based on the findings of the investigation.

#Indore #MadhyaPradesh #ViralVideo #MarriageDispute #Police

articles.title: Kanwar Yatra Tension in Ghaziabad: Youth Assaulted After Pilgrims Allege He Touched Kanwar
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Tension erupted in Uttar Pradesh's Ghaziabad on Thursday after a group of Kanwariyas allegedly assaulted a youth, accusing him of touching their Kanwar, which they claimed broke during the Kanwar Yatra.

body.html:
Tension erupted in Uttar Pradesh's Ghaziabad on Thursday after a group of Kanwariyas allegedly assaulted a youth, accusing him of touching their Kanwar, which they claimed broke during the Kanwar Yatra.

According to reports, the incident occurred around 4 pm in the Madhuban Bapudham police station area. The youth, identified as Imran, was allegedly slapped and punched by the pilgrims after they claimed he touched the Kanwar, violating their religious beliefs.

Police said the Kanwariyas also allegedly held the youth for nearly 20 minutes, leading to a traffic jam stretching about a kilometre near Guldhar railway station as locals gathered at the spot.

Kanwariya Sonu Kumar, a resident of Bharatpur in Rajasthan, said he was returning home with 15 fellow pilgrims after collecting Ganga water from Haridwar. He claimed he had strictly followed the religious rituals throughout the journey and was scheduled to perform Jalabhishek at a Shiva temple in his village on August 11. According to him, the Kanwar broke after the alleged contact, rendering his pilgrimage invalid.

Police reached the spot, pacified the pilgrims and facilitated the ritual worship of the Kanwar in accordance with their religious customs. The pilgrims then resumed their journey, while traffic was restored after the crowd was dispersed.

Additional Police Commissioner (Law and Order) Rajkaran Nayyar said police have been directed to maintain heightened vigilance during the Kanwar Yatra. Authorities have also ordered strict enforcement of traffic diversions and restrictions on heavy vehicles along the Kanwar route between the Meerut and Delhi borders.

Further investigation into the incident is underway.

#Ghaziabad #KanwarYatra #UttarPradesh #BreakingNews

articles.title: Boy Seen Beating Elderly Women at Indore Old Age Home; Administration Moves to Seal Facility
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A video showing a 14-year-old boy allegedly assaulting elderly women with a stick at an old age home in Indore has surfaced on social media, triggering concern over the safety of senior citizens at the facility.

body.html:
A video showing a 14-year-old boy allegedly assaulting elderly women with a stick at an old age home in Indore has surfaced on social media, triggering concern over the safety of senior citizens at the facility.

The incident reportedly occurred at the Maharana Pratap Welfare Society's old age home near Marimata water tank. The video shows the boy beating an elderly woman with a stick and allegedly scuffling with people who attempted to intervene.

According to ACP Rubina Mizwani, the investigation found that the boy's mental condition is reportedly unstable. He had arrived at the old age home with his mother around five months ago. His mother later suffered burn injuries and died, after which the boy remained at the facility.

Police said the incident occurred on Wednesday after the boy allegedly had an argument with an elderly woman and attacked her with a stick.

Banganga police summoned the old age home's director, Neelam Dubey, and released her after issuing a warning. Authorities have also initiated the process of registering an FIR.

Following the incident, Collector Shiv Verma directed the SDM and Tehsildar to inspect the facility. Officials said around 30 elderly people are staying there. Those in good health are being shifted to Nirashrit Ashram and Ganesh Vridh Ashram in Gandhi Nagar, while sick residents will be shifted to a government hospital.

The administration has also initiated the process of sealing the old age home after finding that it was operating illegally.

Officials said the boy will receive counselling and be handed over to Child Line. He is expected to be shifted from the facility and placed in an institution for minors.

The old age home's director, Neelam Dubey, said she was away attending Guru Pujan when the incident occurred. She claimed the boy later told her that the elderly woman had hit him on the head with a tub, following which he attacked her with a stick.

The Social Justice and Women and Child Development departments have been directed to investigate the incident.

#Indore #MadhyaPradesh #OldAgeHome #ElderlySafety

articles.title: Panic at Dakshineswar Station as Overhead Electric Wire Snaps, Train Services Briefly Disrupted
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Panic broke out at Dakshineswar railway station on Wednesday after an overhead electric (OHE) wire snapped, triggering smoke and bright flashes as passengers were arriving at the station.

body.html:
Panic broke out at Dakshineswar railway station on Wednesday after an overhead electric (OHE) wire snapped, triggering smoke and bright flashes as passengers were arriving at the station.

Train services were briefly disrupted while railway personnel carried out repair work and restored the damaged overhead line. No injuries were reported in the incident.

Railway officials said modern electric trains are equipped with multiple safety features, including pantographs, insulators and a metal body that acts as a Faraday cage, helping safely channel stray electrical current and protect passengers during such incidents.

Authorities are investigating the cause of the overhead wire failure. Passengers have been advised to stay away from railway tracks and avoid boarding or alighting from moving trains.

#Dakshineswar #Railway #TrainServices #OHE #WestBengal

articles.title: Missing for Two Years, ‘Australia’ Lie Exposed: Jamnagar Man Allegedly Murdered by Wife and Her Lov
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A man who had been missing for more than two years was allegedly murdered by his wife and her alleged lover, who are accused of poisoning him with cyanide mixed in alcohol before burying his body inside a factory on the outskirts of Gujarat's Jamnagar.

body.html:
A man who had been missing for more than two years was allegedly murdered by his wife and her alleged lover, who are accused of poisoning him with cyanide mixed in alcohol before burying his body inside a factory on the outskirts of Gujarat's Jamnagar.

According to police, the accused concealed the alleged murder by repeatedly telling the victim's family that he had moved to Australia for work.

The case came to light after the victim's brother, Ashok Dharmeshbhai Madhavjibhai Mavdiya, lodged a complaint on July 26.

Police said the victim, Jignesh, had been out of contact with his family for over two years because his wife allegedly claimed he was working in Australia. Whenever relatives sought his contact details, she allegedly told them that the company he worked for did not permit phone calls. She also reportedly claimed he would return to India only after obtaining permanent residency, delaying suspicion for nearly two years.

The matter reportedly unravelled when a cousin of the complainant planned to travel to Australia and asked the woman for Jignesh's contact details. Police said that when she was threatened with legal action, she allegedly confessed to the crime.

Investigators questioned the woman and her alleged lover, Nilesh, for two days. During interrogation, the duo allegedly confessed to murdering Jignesh in May 2024 by mixing cyanide into his alcohol before burying his body in a 12-foot-deep pit inside an abandoned factory that Jignesh and Nilesh had reportedly taken on lease.

Police said an executive magistrate, forensic experts and other officials were present as excavation began at the factory premises to recover the victim's remains.

Further investigation is underway.

#Jamnagar #Gujarat #Murder #CrimeNews #Police

articles.title: ‘I’ll Slap You’: Woman Police Officer Allegedly Threatens Man at Indore Collectorate, Video Surfaces
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A video has surfaced on social media showing a woman police officer allegedly threatening a man at the Collectorate Office in Indore, Madhya Pradesh, during a documentation process.

body.html:
A video has surfaced on social media showing a woman police officer allegedly threatening a man at the Collectorate Office in Indore, Madhya Pradesh, during a documentation process.

According to the account shared with the video, Hitesh Lakhani had visited the office with his wife and waited for around 1.5 hours. When he allegedly asked politely how much longer the process would take, he claims he was ignored while a staff member was scrolling through Instagram.

Lakhani then reportedly approached another official to seek an update. Before he could finish speaking, the woman police officer allegedly told him to sit quietly and threatened to slap him, saying he would not be able to do anything.

The account accompanying the video claims Lakhani was neither shouting nor creating a disturbance and had only sought information after waiting for a considerable time.

The video has sparked questions over the treatment of citizens at government offices. The person who shared the video urged the concerned authorities to investigate the incident and ensure that citizens are treated with dignity and respect.

The authenticity and full context of the video could not be independently verified.

#Indore #MadhyaPradesh #Collectorate #Police

articles.title: Bengaluru Head Constable Assaulted by Youths After Woman Alleges Misbehaviour on BMTC Bus
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A head constable attached to Sanjaynagar Police Station was allegedly assaulted by a group of youths near Gangammanagudi Circle on Tuesday after a woman accused him of behaving inappropriately with her on a BMTC bus.

body.html:
A head constable attached to Sanjaynagar Police Station was allegedly assaulted by a group of youths near Gangammanagudi Circle on Tuesday after a woman accused him of behaving inappropriately with her on a BMTC bus.

According to preliminary information, Head Constable Manjunath had boarded a BMTC bus heading towards Jalahalli when he allegedly misbehaved with a woman passenger. An argument reportedly broke out inside the bus, following which the woman informed her relatives.

When the bus reached Gangammanagudi Circle, a group of youths allegedly intercepted Manjunath and assaulted him. Police said the attackers continued beating him even after he identified himself as a police officer.

Manjunath sustained bleeding injuries to his face and bruises, while his clothes were reportedly torn during the assault. He was later admitted to a private hospital for treatment.

The woman has filed a complaint against Manjunath alleging inappropriate behaviour, while the head constable has lodged a counter-complaint against the youths for assault.

Police have registered separate cases based on both complaints and are investigating the incident.

#Bengaluru #Karnataka #BMTC #Police #HeadConstable

articles.title: Egg Argument Turns Deadly in Jaipur: MP Man Beaten to Death With Sticks, Four Detained
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A minor argument over eggs falling on the road allegedly turned fatal in Jaipur's Mansarovar area after a 23-year-old man from Madhya Pradesh was beaten to death with sticks.

body.html:
A minor argument over eggs falling on the road allegedly turned fatal in Jaipur's Mansarovar area after a 23-year-old man from Madhya Pradesh was beaten to death with sticks. A video of the assault has surfaced on social media, showing four youths carrying sticks and one of them striking the victim on the head from behind.

The deceased has been identified as Balveer, a native of Sheopur in Madhya Pradesh, who worked in the marble and tiles business while living on rent in the Gurjar Ki Thadi area of Jaipur. His brother, Ramveer, lodged a murder complaint at Mansarovar police station.

According to police, the incident occurred on Tuesday evening after a dispute broke out when eggs being carried by one of the accused reportedly fell on the road following a collision with Balveer. The argument escalated, and the accused allegedly attacked Balveer with sticks. Two others present at the scene also sustained injuries.

Police said the accused had allegedly been consuming alcohol before the incident. During the investigation, it emerged that the group, including a minor, assaulted Balveer before fleeing the spot.

Locals rushed the injured to Jaipuria Hospital. As Balveer's condition deteriorated, he was shifted to SMS Hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries at around 11.30 pm on Tuesday.

Jaipur South DCP Rajarshi Raj said four accused, including a minor, have been detained. The arrested accused have been identified as Manish Solanki (23), Ramzan Ali (19) and Rohit Yadav (19). Police said Ramzan Ali and Manish Solanki already have criminal cases registered against them.

Police are questioning the accused and examining all evidence, including the viral video, to establish the exact sequence of events. Further investigation is underway.

Balveer is survived by his wife and three children, who live in Sheopur, Madhya Pradesh.

#Jaipur #Rajasthan #Murder #CrimeNews #ViralVideo

articles.title: What's Your Rate?': Bengaluru Fruit Seller Arrested After Woman Records Alleged Street Harassment
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A 42-year-old fruit seller from NRI Layout has been arrested for allegedly sexually harassing a woman in Bengaluru's Ramamurthy Nagar by asking, "What's your rate?" while she was waiting for a cab.

body.html:
A 42-year-old fruit seller from NRI Layout has been arrested for allegedly sexually harassing a woman in Bengaluru's Ramamurthy Nagar by asking, "What's your rate?" while she was waiting for a cab.

According to police, the woman recorded part of the incident on her mobile phone and later shared the video on social media, describing how she felt intimidated and objectified while simply trying to return home from work.

She alleged that the accused made sexually offensive remarks, propositioned her for money and attempted to intimidate her, leaving her concerned for her safety.

Acting on the woman's complaint and the video evidence, Ramamurthy Nagar Police traced the accused through the registration number of his scooter (KA 03 KQ 6190). The vehicle was impounded, and the accused, identified as Vijay Raghav, was taken into custody.

Police registered an FIR and booked the accused under Sections 75 and 79 before arresting him. Further investigation is underway.

In her social media post, the woman called for swift police action, stressing that harassment in public spaces should not be normalised. Police said the case highlights the role of video evidence in enabling prompt action against street harassment.

#Bengaluru #RamamurthyNagar #StreetHarassment
